_readme: MUTATION CATALOG — the structural guard for 'tests that pass for the wrong reason' (issue #112).
Each entry names ONE security-critical mechanism, an exact anchor string in the source that
IS that mechanism, a mutation that removes it, and the test files that CLAIM to cover it.
`node scripts/mutation-guard.mjs` applies each mutation in turn, runs only the claimed tests,
and reports SURVIVED for any mutant those tests still pass against. A survivor is not a bug in
the source — it is a hole in the tests, which is the thing #112 found six of.
`packages/core/test/mutation-catalog.test.ts` runs in the ordinary `pnpm test` and asserts that
every `anchor` still occurs EXACTLY ONCE in its `file`, and that every `tests` path exists. That
is what keeps this catalog from rotting into a no-op: a refactor that moves a mechanism breaks
the catalog loudly instead of silently turning its mutant into a no-op edit.
MOSTLY security-critical mechanisms, and one (#152) that is not: whether capwall's ESM install
starts Node's module-customization THREAD is a startup-cost invariant. It earns a mutant on the
same argument the security ones do — going back to `module.register()` breaks nothing and fails
nothing, and silently puts ~53 ms of thread bootstrap back on every mediated process (and, on
Node 26, a DEP0205 warning on stderr). A property no test asserts is a property that decays,
`needsBuild` marks mutants whose claimed tests spawn a subprocess against `dist/` — those need
a rebuild after mutating and after restoring.

mutants.mechanism: #21 — collapse runs of `**` segments so a glob compiles to ONE unbounded group (ReDoS hardening)
mutants.note: The #112 item-1 regression anchor. SURVIVED before #112; must stay CAUGHT.

mutants.mechanism: #106/#120 — every segment at or after the first magic segment must be provably downward-only; anything not proven bounded is unbounded (fail closed to the filesystem root)
#120 — an unbalanced brace is a construct capwall refuses to expand, so the pattern is unbounded rather than parsed optimistically
mutants.mutation: if (false && close === -1) return null; // unbalanced open

mutants.mechanism: policy evaluation reads grants as OWN properties only, so a polluted Object.prototype cannot inject a grant into the empty deny-by-default grant
#49/#99 — a `.node` load is charged to BOTH the caller and the package that owns the addon file; caller-only makes a shared resolver a skeleton key
#99 — the dlopen filename argument is stringified ONCE and the pinned string is forwarded, so a toString that answers twice cannot load a file the gate never saw
mutants.anchor:
const converted = String(raw); // the ONE conversion — Node's `node::Utf8Value`, in JS
    return { path: normalizeAddonPath(converted), forward: converted };

mutants.mechanism: #60 — an unattributable call charges `<unknown>`, an ordinary deny-by-default principal, and NOT the exempt `<app>` trust root
#17 — hardened mode freezes the shim namespaces capwall hands out, so `fs.readFileSync = evil` cannot remove a guard
#17/#70 — hardened mode freezes guarded SUBCLASSES and their prototypes, closing `net.Socket.prototype.connect = evil`
mutants.anchor:
if (ctx.hardened !== true) return;
  if (typeof Cls !== "function") return;

mutants.mechanism: #97 — a hardened install pins the capwall-installed global egress functions writable:false, even when an un-hardened install built them
mutants.anchor: slot.pin(replacement); // best-effort — a global someone made non-configurable is reported below

mutants.mechanism: #98 — the env-gate suspension during a real spawn is scoped to the exact keys Node itself reads, not a blanket 'gate off' window
#60/#86 — the dgram auto-bind replay token is single-use, so a dependency that reads `socket.send` cannot keep an un-gated send around
#133/#143 — when the shortened capture reaches nothing it may believe, attribution re-runs the VERBATIM full walk; 'found nothing' is never an answer, and never the `<app>` trust root
mutants.note: The fail-open the boundary fast path could reintroduce: three nested evals fill the whole prefix with OPAQUE frames, and a decline that answers `<app>` hands the trust root to any dependency willing to call eval.

mutants.mechanism: #133/#143 — the fast path stands down entirely below the frame budget at which 'the short capture found it' still implies 'the full capture would have found it too', rather than offering a second opinion the full walk could not reach
#143 — capwall's OWN frames are never a principal. V8 skips them on the fast path and the walk skips them on the fallback; the two must agree, or a declined capture attributes the shim itself
mutants.anchor: if (source.startsWith(CAPWALL_ROOT + path.sep)) continue; // capwall's own machinery
mutants.mutation: if (false && source.startsWith(CAPWALL_ROOT + path.sep)) continue; // capwall's own machinery
mutants.note: Only observable on the FALLBACK path, which is exactly why it needs a mutant: the fast path skips those frames in V8 and would hide the loss.

mutants.mechanism: #152/#153 — capwall's ESM interception uses the SYNCHRONOUS module.registerHooks(), so no module-customization thread is started (~53 ms) and no DEP0205 deprecation warning is printed. module.register() is Stability 0 with removal announced
mutants.anchor: hooks = realModule.registerHooks({ resolve, load }) as RegisteredHooks;
mutants.mutation:
hooks = realModule.registerHooks({ resolve, load }) as RegisteredHooks;
    realModule.register("data:text/javascript,export function resolve(s,c,n){return n(s,c)}", import.meta.url);
mutants.note: The one mutant in this catalog that ADDS rather than removes, because the invariant is an absence. It re-creates exactly the cost #152 removed — the loader thread — without changing a single behaviour, which is why nothing but a dedicated probe catches it.

mutants.mechanism: #62/#152 — the LAST uninstall() deregisters the module hooks, so ESM teardown is real rather than best-effort and a never-imported specifier is un-mediated afterwards exactly as it is on the CJS path, instead of throwing a bridge error that permanently poisons the specifier
mutants.note: module.register() could not offer this line at all — the asymmetry docs/threat-model.md used to carry as a known limit. Without it the hooks outlive their install and #62's swap fixture reports the pre-#152 behaviour.

mutants.mechanism: #152 — the ESM resolve hook stands down for the #123 module-read decision ONLY when loader/require.ts already took it: inside a gated Module._load AND for a `require` export condition. require(esm) pulls a whole ES subgraph in synchronously inside one Module._load, so the depth test alone would disarm the gate for every import below it
mutants.note: Fail-OPEN in one direction (a laundered import goes un-gated) and merely noisy in the other (two decisions for one require), which is why the conjunction is the conservative form and both halves are asserted.

mutants.mechanism: #78/#61 — the load hook re-mediates any raw node:<mediated> URL it is handed, since capwall's own resolve never emits one. Since #152 this is reachable only from a SYNCHRONOUS hook registered after capwall's, which is the one attacker position still ahead of capwall in the chain
mutants.note: Had no mutant while the register() chain also reached it and two tests covered it. It now has exactly one route and one test, so it needs one.
